title: Talking About Family
goal: Describe family relationships and contact, ask a useful follow-up, or keep personal information private.

study.title: Ask and give a short account

runs.text: Chapter 14 supplies relationship words. For this chapter, a small set is enough:
, and any relationship that matters to your account.
I have an older brother and a younger sister.
Describe the relationship and age order.
Identify your position among the children.

runs.text: is a short answer meaning she lives nearby. You can use the full sentence if that is easier.
Are you close to your family?
asks about the relationship, not just physical distance. People can be close emotionally and live far apart.
I see my parents twice a month.
We're not in touch right now.
Say you are not communicating now.

signals that there is more to it; it does not supply the details.

runs.text: , and other family names depend on the person's family. You can say
introduces the person using your family name for her. You do not need to replace the name your family actually uses.
Family questions can be personal. You can give a short answer, change the subject, or state that you do not want to discuss it.

turns.speaker: Miles

runs.text: No. I'd rather not talk about that right now.

turns.en: No. I'd rather not talk about that right now.

turns.speaker: Hana

runs.text: Okay. No problem. How's your class going?

turns.en: Okay. No problem. How's your class going?

runs.text: is also available if you intend a firm boundary. You can ask
Would you rather talk about something else?
when the other person's response leaves you unsure. A short answer is not an invitation to demand an explanation.

practice.title: Give only the details you choose

runs.text: You have an older brother and a younger sister. Your sister lives nearby. Your brother lives far away. You speak to him once a week. You and your sister get along well.
Include your place among the three children.
Are you close to your brother?
Your role feels close despite the distance. Supply a reason from the profile.
Change the role: you are an only child. Answer without using the first profile's siblings.
Change the intention: you do not want to discuss your family. Rehearse a boundary and the other person's acknowledgment. Support:
I'd rather not talk about my family
Hide the profile. Give a short true or invented family account using three details. On your own, then ask and answer one follow-up that stays within those details.
Yes. I have an older brother and a younger sister. I'm the middle child.
My sister lives nearby, but my brother lives far away.
Yes. We talk once a week even though he lives far away.
I'd rather not talk about my family right now. — Okay. Let's talk about something else.
Did you describe actual relationships and contact? Did your follow-up fit the information given? Could you participate without revealing details you wanted to keep private?

vocabulary.ja: そのことは話したくありません

ja: 家族について、話す範囲を選ぶ。
note: 関係と、会う頻度や親しさは別です。話したくない内容なら、無理に詳しく説明せず境界を伝えられます。
